title: Feature gates experiment: flexible observability retention & streamlined security questionnaire
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a multi-armed pricing and gating experiment to evaluate flexible observability retention as a metered add-on combined with a simplified security questionnaire intake flow and premium SLA gating. Goal is to determine willingness to pay for retention beyond default (30 days), understand contract friction caused by SQ (security questionnaire) complexity, and validate gating logic for premium SLA entitlement in the contract flow.
hypothesis: Providing a granular, price-sensitive observability retention add-on (e.g., 30d free, 90d/365d paid tiers) plus an inline, auto-filled security questionnaire flow will increase conversion for enterprise trials into paid add-on attachments by at least 15% and reduce average sales cycle time by 10% for customers requiring compliance documentation. Premium SLA gating will not materially reduce trials but will increase ARR for qualifying accounts.
experiment_design: Three-arm experiment across new enterprise trials: (A) Control: current static retention + manual SQ; (B) Retention tiers: UI offering 90d and 365d as purchasable add-ons + manual SQ; (C) Retention tiers + automated SQ pre-fill + explicit SLA gating checkbox with entitlement check. Pricing matrix will test 2 price points per extended retention tier. Entitlement flags will be surfaced via the entitlement API. Success defined on primary and secondary metrics tracked for 90-day window.
rollout_plan: Week 1: feature flag gated release to 10 targeted pilot orgs (sales-sourced). Week 2-6: expand to 100 organically recruited enterprise trials across NA/EU with even split across arms. Weekly telemetry review and interim decision point at week 3. Week 7: freeze and analyze 30/60/90 day cohorts. Deliver go/no-go recommendation to Commercial Leadership and Legal for wider rollout.
